questions.q: The TOGAF Standard describes Enterprise Architecture principally as a means to do which of the following?
o: Guide effective and efficient change toward the enterprise's target outcomes
Catalog every server and application in use
Replace the role of project management
questions.e: The purpose of EA is to guide effective, efficient, agile, and durable change in pursuit of the enterprise's goals and target outcomes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a commonly cited benefit of having an Enterprise Architecture?
o: It guarantees that no projects will ever fail
It removes the need for governance
questions.e: Benefits include faster/simpler/cheaper procurement, better strategic decisions, higher return on investment, and reduced risk on future investment.

questions.q: Which architecture domain describes the structure of an organization's conceptual, logical, and physical data assets?
questions.e: The Data Architecture describes the structure of conceptual, logical, and physical data assets and data management resources.

questions.q: Along the Architecture Continuum, how are assets arranged?
questions.e: The Architecture Continuum ranges from generic Foundation Architectures to Organization-Specific Architectures; generic assets are adapted to create specific ones.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository holds the record of governance activity such as decision logs and compliance assessments?
questions.e: The Governance Repository records governance activity: decision logs, compliance assessments, and capability assessments.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the TOGAF definition of risk?
o: A certain future loss to the enterprise
The effect of uncertainty on objectives, with a probability and an impact
A stakeholder concern that has been ignored
questions.e: Risk is the effect of uncertainty on objectives; it is not certain and has both a probability/frequency and an impact.

questions.q: How many phases sit inside the main ADM cycle (labelled A to H)?
questions.e: Eight phases (A through H) sit in the cycle; the Preliminary Phase precedes it and Requirements Management sits in the centre.

questions.q: A deliverable marked 'draft' means which of the following?
o: It has been reviewed and formally approved
It is under development with no formal review or approval yet
It has been archived in the repository
questions.e: Draft means under development with no formal review or approval yet; approved means reviewed and approved, but not necessarily finalized.

questions.q: Which statement about the steps within each ADM phase is correct?
o: They are mandatory and must be followed in strict order
They are recommendations that should be tailored under governance
They apply only to Phase A
questions.e: The steps within each phase are recommendations, not mandates; they are tailored to the situation under architecture governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of the Preliminary Phase?
o: Define the organizational model and select architecture tools
Perform the gap analysis for the Technology Architecture
questions.e: Preliminary Phase objectives include determining and establishing the Architecture Capability: defining the organizational model, governance, principles, and selecting tools.

questions.q: Which deliverable, created in Phase A, serves as the contract between the architecture team and the sponsor and defines the scope and approach?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work is developed in the last step of Phase A, defines scope and approach, and acts as a contract between the architecture team and sponsor.

questions.q: Which architecture is developed in Phase D?
questions.e: Phase D develops the baseline and target Technology Architecture (logical software and hardware infrastructure capabilities and standards).

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Phase E, Opportunities and Solutions?
o: To finalize the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan
To perform initial implementation planning and identify delivery vehicles
questions.e: Phase E performs initial implementation planning, identifies delivery vehicles (programs, projects, portfolios), and determines Transition Architectures. The detailed plan is finalized in Phase F.

questions.q: Which deliverable is created in Phase F to enable governance within the implementation projects?
questions.e: The Implementation Governance Model is created in Phase F to enable architecture governance within implementation projects; it is applied in Phase G.

questions.q: According to the TOGAF Standard, in which phase does the method explicitly align with Agile development?
questions.e: TOGAF aligns with Agile development in Phase G, where the EA sets constraints and guardrails for product owners and agile teams.

questions.q: Phase H, Architecture Change Management, is characterized as which of the following?
o: The phase that creates the Statement of Architecture Work
A holding phase that keeps the ADM running
The phase that develops the Data Architecture
The phase that establishes the Architecture Capability
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase that keeps the ADM running and decides whether a change is a light update or warrants a new ADM cycle.

questions.q: Which artifact provides a single point of truth for all agreed, reviewed, and approved requirements?
questions.e: Requirements Management maintains the requirements baseline, a snapshot of all agreed/reviewed/approved requirements, as the single point of truth.

questions.q: How do the ADM and the supporting Guidelines and Techniques relate?
o: The Guidelines and Techniques replace the ADM
The Guidelines and Techniques support the application of the ADM
The ADM is a technique within the Guidelines
questions.e: The supporting Guidelines and Techniques support the application of the ADM; techniques such as gap analysis and risk management are used across phases.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the four sections of the TOGAF architecture principle template?
questions.e: The template is Name, Statement, Rationale, Implications. Name is the label, Statement is the rule, Rationale is the business benefit, Implications are the requirements to carry it out.

questions.q: Which criterion requires that a principle's intentions are clear and unambiguous so that violations are minimized?
questions.e: Understandable means the principle's intentions are clear and unambiguous, minimizing violations. The five criteria are Understandable, Robust, Complete, Consistent, Stable.

questions.q: In which ADM phase is the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment primarily applied?
questions.e: The BTRA is applied in Phase A to evaluate the organization's readiness to undergo change; its mitigations feed into the roadmap and Implementation and Migration Plan (E/F).

questions.q: According to the notes, which is the most critical source of gaps in an architecture?
questions.e: Ignored stakeholder concerns are the most critical source of gaps; gaps are shortfalls (deliberate, accidental, or open) between baseline and target across all four domains.

questions.q: TOGAF divides architecture risk into which categories?
questions.e: TOGAF classifies architecture risks by type as time (schedule), cost (budget), and scope. These align to standard project risk categories. Initial and residual are the two risk levels.

questions.q: Which Series Guide covers using the TOGAF Standard to support the Digital Enterprise?
o: G217, Using the TOGAF Standard in the Digital Enterprise
A Practitioner's Approach to Developing EA
questions.e: Support for the Digital Enterprise is new in TOGAF 10 and covered by Series Guide G217, 'Using the TOGAF Standard in the Digital Enterprise.'

questions.q: Which landscape level has the broadest breadth, lowest detail, and longest time horizon?
questions.e: The Strategic level is enterprise-wide with low detail and a long time horizon for executive direction setting. Segment is medium; Capability is narrow and detailed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of architecture partitioning?
o: It removes the need for an Architecture Board
It enables parallelization of work across teams
It guarantees a single target architecture
questions.e: Partitioning benefits include conflict management, parallelization of work, reuse, and reduced complexity with effective governance.

questions.q: Why does the TOGAF Standard recommend considering architecture alternatives?
o: Because a single valid target architecture never exists
Because presenting alternatives surfaces hidden agendas, new principles, or requirements and supports trade-off
Because it is mandatory to build every alternative
Because it removes the need for stakeholder approval
questions.e: There can be multiple valid target architectures; presenting alternatives surfaces hidden agendas, new principles or requirements, and supports trade-off among competing forces.

questions.q: Why must the ADM itself be governed?
o: Because the ADM creates and changes the EA, and without governance you cannot tell whether projects move toward the target
Because governance replaces the need for stakeholders
Because governance produces the Architecture Vision
questions.e: The ADM creates, develops, and maintains the EA (a change); without governance you cannot confirm whether projects are moving toward the target architecture.

questions.q: Where do decision rights over the target architecture ultimately reside?
questions.e: Decision rights over the target architecture always lie with the stakeholders. The Board owns the processes and recommendations; the architect assesses and stakeholders approve.

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of Architecture Contract?
questions.e: The Architecture Design and Development Contract, agreed with partners such as system integrators and application providers, is one of the types of Architecture Contract.

questions.q: When an Architecture Compliance Review identifies non-conformance, which of the following is a valid recommendation the architect can make?
o: Provide temporary relief through a dispensation
Delete the target architecture without approval
Reassign decision rights to the architect
questions.e: On non-conformance the architect can recommend enforcing compliance, granting temporary relief (a dispensation), or changing the target architecture.

questions.q: A view is best described as which of the following?
o: A generic, reusable lens stored in a library
A representation of the system from the perspective of a related set of concerns
A contract between sponsor and architect
questions.e: A view is a representation of the system from the perspective of a related set of concerns, built from a viewpoint; it consists of one or more architecture models.

questions.q: How do concerns relate to requirements in the TOGAF Standard?
questions.e: Concerns are stakeholder interests; identifying them ensures stakeholder interests become requirements, so concerns lead to requirements.

questions.q: A Solution Building Block (SBB) is best described as which of the following?
o: A physical, implementation-specific component that delivers the solution
questions.e: An SBB is a physical, implementation-specific component (e.g. a configured product) that delivers the solution; the ABB is logical and supplier-independent.

questions.q: Which deliverable lists work packages on a timeline to show progression from the Baseline to the Target Architecture?
questions.e: The Architecture Roadmap shows progression from baseline to target as work packages on a timeline; it is first produced in Phase E and confirmed in Phase F.

questions.q: Which deliverable is the trigger sent from the sponsoring organization to start an architecture development cycle?
questions.e: The Request for Architecture Work is sent from the sponsoring organization to the architecture team to trigger a cycle; it is a primary output of the Preliminary Phase.

questions.q: In step 6 of ADM Requirements Management, where are changed requirements' impacts assessed and the Requirements Impact Assessment reissued as version n+1?
o: Within the Requirements Management process alone
questions.e: The step 6 activities belong to the relevant ADM phase: assess current and previous phase impacts, decide implementation or deferral, and issue the updated impact assessment. Requirements Management also generates an impact assessment in step 5; it is not excluded from producing the deliverable.

questions.q: Which deliverable requests a dispensation or kick-starts a further cycle of architecture work and is the key input to Phase H?
questions.e: A Change Request requests a dispensation or kick-starts a further cycle of architecture work; it is the most important architectural input to Phase H.

questions.q: In which ADM phase is the Enterprise Metamodel customized for the organization?
questions.e: The Enterprise Metamodel is enterprise-specific and is customized in the Preliminary Phase as part of tailoring the framework.

questions.q: Which best describes an Architecture Capability?
o: A business capability for architecture: the structures, roles, skills, responsibilities, and processes to do EA
questions.e: An Architecture Capability is a business capability for architecture, put in place through organization structures, roles, skills, responsibilities, and processes, run like any operational unit.
